Narrative and Plans

Type 1 Zoning Narrative for
3000-3010 N. Elbridge
B3-2 and RS3 to B3-2

A. The applicant proposes to rezone the subject property from B3-2 Community
Shopping-Use District and RS3 Residential Single-Unit (Detached House) District B3-2
Community Shopping District. A portion of the subject property (3000 N. Elbridge) is
the site of the existing Puerto Rican Arts Alliance (“PRAA”) building. The reminder of
the site are previously occupied residential! buildings. The purpose of the amendment is
to allow the entire subject property to be used by PRAA as a community center. PRAA
will operate culturally enriching and transforming programs, performances, exhibits and
events at the site.

The applicant will seek a special use for the community center subsequent to a
successful rezoning.

The subject property is a Transit Serviced Location based on proximity to Milwaukee
Avenue (approximately 125 feet) and the Belmont Blue line station (approximately
1747 feet).

In accordance with Section 1 7-3-0308, any new construction within 2,640 feet of a CTA
or METRA rail station entrance or exit must satisfy all of the following specific criteria.
The proposed project satisfies such criteria as noted below:

1, The project complies with the applicable standards of Section 17-10-0102-B.
0 This criterion is met because the subject property is a Transit-Served
Location as noted above.

2. The project complies with the standards and regulations of Section 17-3-0504,
except paragraph H if the project is not located along a pedestrian street, pertaining to
pedestrian streets and pedestrian retail streets, even if the project is not located along a
pedestrian street or a pedestrian retail street.

o This criterion is met. 24th Boulevard is not a pedestrian street and the
proposed land use is in a non-commercial use group, therefore, paragraph
H does not apply.

o Paragraph B is met by the variation requested with this application.

o Paragraph C is met.

o Paragraph D is met because the primary entrance is on Elbridge Street.

o Paragraph E is not applicable.

o Paragraph F is met with the parking to the rear of the proposed building.

o Paragraph G is met because vehicle access comes from the alley.

o Paragraphs I and J are not applicable.

3. The project complies with the general goals set forth in the Transit Friendly
Development Guide: Station Area Typology, and any other station-specific plans,
designs or guidelines adopted by the Chicago Plan Commission.

o The Guide defines “Transit Friendly Development” as “Development
which is oriented towards and integrated with adjacent transit. The
development incorporates accessibility and connectivity and is a multiuse
mix of dense development that generates significant levels of transit
riders.” The proposed development is integrated with adjacent transit
and benefit from proximity to transit.

4. Residential building projects shall not have a number of parking spaces in excess
of 50% of the Minimum Automobile Parking Ratio for the applicable district listed in
Section 17-10-0207 with any fractional result rounded up to the next higher whole
number, unless additional parking spaces are approved as an administrative adjustment
under the provisions of Section 17-13-1003-EE.

© This standard is met.

5. The project complies with the Travel Demand Study and Management Plan
rules of the Chicago Department of Transportation. The City's Commissioner of
Transportation is authorized to issue Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules
consistent with this section.

o The project will comply with these standards.

The applicant is seeking the following relief: (i) a variation in accordance with Section
17-13-0303-D to reduce parking from thirteen (13) to four (4) in accordance with
Sections 17-10-0207-Q, 17-10-0102-B.
